title: Object pronouns
tagline: Lo, la, le, se lo: it, him, her, to them… and where they go.
goal: Replace nouns with direct (lo, la, los, las) and indirect (le, les) object pronouns, combine them (se lo) and place them correctly.

sections.title: Direct objects: lo, la, los, las

blocks.text: Direct object pronouns replace the thing or person that receives the action. They agree with the noun they replace and go **before the conjugated verb**:

blocks.title: The personal «a»
blocks.text: A specific person as direct object takes *a*: *Veo {a} María* → *{La} veo*. Things don't: *Veo la casa*.
Indirect objects say **to whom** or **for whom**: *le* (to him / her / you-usted), *les* (to them). Spanish usually keeps the pronoun even when the person is named:

items.tr: I gave my mom a present.
Did you write to your grandparents?

blocks.text: indirect + direct · le / les + lo / la → se lo / se la

items.tr: The book? I'll lend it to you.

items.fr: ¿Las fotos? {Se las} mando a mis padres.
items.tr: The photos? I'll send them to my parents.
The bill? Could you bring it to me, please?

blocks.title: Where they go
blocks.text: Before a conjugated verb: *te lo doy*. Attached to an infinitive, a gerund or a positive command: *voy a dártelo, estoy diciéndotelo, dámelo*. Add an accent to keep the stress.

exercises.title: Lo, la, los, las
exercises.instructions: Replace the noun with a pronoun.

items.prompt: ¿Ves a tus primas? Sí, ___ veo los domingos.
___ di un regalo a mi mamá.
___ escribo a mis abuelos cada mes.
___ explico la tarea a los niños.

exercises.title: Two pronouns
exercises.instructions: Replace both objects. Choose the right combination.

items.prompt: Te presto el libro. → Te ___ presto.
Le mando las fotos a mi papá. → ___ mando.
Les doy el dinero a ellos. → ___ doy.
I gave it (the book) to him.
I'm going to buy it (the shirt).

checklist: I replace things and people with lo, la, los, las.
I use le / les for «to someone», even when the person is named.
I change le / les to se before lo / la: se lo.
I attach pronouns to infinitives and positive commands.

challenge.title: Gifts
challenge.text: Write five sentences about presents you gave or received, using double pronouns: *¿El reloj? Me lo regaló mi abuela. ¿Las flores? Se las compré a mi mamá.*
